results.criterion: Similar types of information are presented in similar, consistent ways.
results.rationale: Consistency of similar information does not pass Repeated information families vary substantially across pages or templates. Recommendation: Standardize repeated visual families such as headings, buttons, links, cards, and labels.

results.criterion: The UI uses no more than 3 primary colors.
results.rationale: Primary color count does not pass At least one page relies on too many dominant accent color families. Recommendation: Reduce the number of dominant accent color families and treat nearby tonal shades as a single system.

results.criterion: The UI “chrome” is made up of de-saturated colors that recede visually so content comes immediately into focus.
results.rationale: UI chrome desaturation does not pass At least one page has supporting UI chrome that competes too strongly with content or actions. Recommendation: Reduce saturation on utility surfaces, navigation chrome, borders, and secondary backgrounds.

results.criterion: Colors help establish reinforce the hierarchy of content and interactive elements.
results.rationale: Color hierarchy reinforcement does not pass At least one page does not use color strongly enough to support hierarchy and action emphasis. Recommendation: Reserve stronger accent colors for primary actions and hierarchy-critical elements.

results.criterion: The color scheme is used consistently throughout the application or web site.
results.rationale: Color scheme consistency is moderate Cross-page palettes show partial consistency, but some templates diverge noticeably. Recommendation: Review shared palette tokens across templates and align accent families site-wide.

results.criterion: Colors are not over-saturated and don’t vibrate or fatigue the eye.
results.rationale: Some oversaturated colors were detected Some pages include highly saturated colors that may feel visually aggressive in context. Recommendation: Reduce saturation on dominant accent colors and large surfaces, reserving intense colors for small intentional accents.

results.criterion: Items with the most contrast are also the most important items on the screen, both to the user and/or the business.
results.rationale: Priority contrast criterion passes Higher-priority elements generally receive at least comparable or stronger contrast treatment.

results.criterion: Contrast is the primary mechanism for establishing visual priority/hierarchy.
results.rationale: Hierarchy contrast criterion is moderate Some pages rely on hierarchy cues, but contrast contributes only moderately. Recommendation: Increase contrast separation between headings, key labels, and body content while preserving a coherent type scale.

results.criterion: Contrast is the primary mechanism for visually separating content from controls (e.g. buttons, links, menus)
results.rationale: Control separation contrast criterion does not pass At least one page includes low-contrast controls that do not stand apart strongly enough from content. Recommendation: Increase contrast on buttons, links, and action triggers so they stand apart more clearly from nearby content.

results.criterion: Contrast is the primary mechanism used to separate labels from the content or data they describe.
results.rationale: Label/content contrast separation could not be evaluated There were too few label/content elements to evaluate this criterion reliably.

results.criterion: Foreground elements (content and controls) are easily distinguished from the background.
results.rationale: Foreground/background distinction does not pass At least one page shows weak foreground/background contrast likely to reduce readability or discoverability. Recommendation: Strengthen text and control contrast against their effective background surfaces.

results.criterion: No more than two (2) distinct font families are used (e.g. Helvetica & Times).
results.rationale: Font family count passes Rendered text usage appears limited to a restrained set of font families.

results.criterion: Fonts used for content are at least 12 pixels in size.
results.rationale: Minimum content font size passes No strong evidence of undersized rendered content text was found.

results.criterion: Font size and weight is used to differentiate between content types (e.g. Headings, subheadings, paragraphs).
results.rationale: Typography differentiation does not pass At least one page does not show meaningful typographic separation between headings and content. Recommendation: Increase size and/or weight separation between headings, subheadings, and paragraph text.

results.criterion: Font styles, sizes and weights are used consistently throughout every screen.
results.rationale: Cross-screen font consistency passes The audited pages generally use a stable set of typography families, sizes, and weights.

results.criterion: Font styles, sizes and weights establish and reinforce the hierarchy of content.
results.rationale: Font hierarchy reinforcement does not pass At least one page has typography that does not support hierarchy strongly enough. Recommendation: Define a clearer type scale so headings, content, and controls form a stronger hierarchy system.

results.criterion: Different font styles (or families) are used to separate labels from content.
results.rationale: Label/content typography separation is not applicable There were too few usable label elements to evaluate this criterion reliably.

results.criterion: Different font styles (or families) are used to separate content from controls.
results.rationale: Content/control typography separation does not pass At least one page does not show enough typographic separation between content and controls. Recommendation: Use stronger size, weight, casing, spacing, or family rules to distinguish interactive text from body content.
